options.name: Kimi For Coding/Kimi For Coding HighSpeed
build
options.description: The default agent. Executes tools based on configured permissions.

options.name: plan
options.description: Plan mode. Disallows all edit tools.

availableCommands.name: api-tokens
availableCommands.description: Manages the centralized age-encrypted API token store at ~/.config/tokens/tokens.env.age. Use when reading, adding, editing, removing, or syncing API keys and bot tokens across local projects and the VPS (yiin.lt).

availableCommands.name: apple-design
availableCommands.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.

availableCommands.name: axi
availableCommands.description: Agent eXperience Interface (AXI) — ergonomic standards for building CLI tools that agents use via shell execution. Use when building, modifying, or reviewing any agent-facing CLI.

availableCommands.name: beads
availableCommands.description: Use when working in a repository that uses bd or Beads for durable project task tracking, issue dependencies, blocker management, multi-session handoff, or shared work memory. Trigger when the user asks to find ready work, claim or close tasks, create follow-up work, inspect blockers, recover project context, or choose between local planning and persistent project tracking.

availableCommands.name: check
availableCommands.description: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then delegate fixes to a separate agent. Use when the user types /check, or when an agent has finished editing code and wants it reviewed before committing or handing back.

availableCommands.name: codebase-design
availableCommands.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

availableCommands.name: cook-epic
availableCommands.description: Execute a beads epic unattended with fresh-context workers on the shared epic core: a three-worker pool with per-worker worktrees and a merge queue by default, or one worker at a time on the base branch. Use when the user types /cook-epic followed by an epic id, or asks to run/execute a beads epic.

availableCommands.name: cook-it
availableCommands.description: Cook a task end-to-end — plan when the instructions leave choices open → critique the plan when it warrants it → implement → review the implementation at a depth matched to its size and nature → quality gate → commit & push. Use when the user types `/cook-it <task>` (e.g. `/cook-it vangrd-uqi2`, `/cook-it fix the cascade in foo.ts`). Suitable for well-scoped engineering tasks where the path is clear enough to commit to but worth double-checking via independent agents. Given a beads epic id, it instead runs one iteration of that epic's Handoff Protocol — cook the top ready child, then update the epic.

availableCommands.name: create-pr
availableCommands.description: Open a pull request whose description leads with a password-protected ht-ml.app explainer built with lavish - ASD-STE100 wording, real diagrams, layout verified headless. Use when the user types /create-pr, or asks to open a PR with a visual explainer page.

availableCommands.name: customize-opencode
availableCommands.description: Use ONLY when the user is editing or creating opencode's own configuration: opencode.json, opencode.jsonc, files under .opencode/, or files under ~/.config/opencode/. Also use when creating or fixing opencode agents, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers, or permission rules. Do not use for the user's own application code, or for any project that is not configuring opencode itself.

availableCommands.name: deploy
availableCommands.description: Commit, push, build, and restart the self-hosted T3 Code checkout on yiin-lt, travel-laptop, and main-laptop. Use when the user says `/deploy`, asks to deploy T3 Code, requests a rebuild and restart, or wants every available T3 Code host synchronized to the same `mine` commit.

availableCommands.name: domain-modeling
availableCommands.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.

availableCommands.name: explain
availableCommands.description: Re-explain your last response in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English — short sentences, simple words, one topic per paragraph. Use when the user types /explain after a fix proposal, plan, or technical answer they want restated for a fast, unambiguous read.

availableCommands.name: find-animation-opportunities
availableCommands.description: Search a codebase or UI for places that don't animate but should, and reject everything that shouldn't. Read-only; it proposes motion with exact values, it does not implement it. Use when the user asks "what could be animated here?" or wants to "make this feel more alive". For fixing existing animations, use improve-animations or review-animations instead.

availableCommands.name: focused
availableCommands.description: Write the minimum code that works — climb the ladder (YAGNI → stdlib → platform → installed deps → one line → minimal code) before writing anything, and refuse to be lazy about the things that matter. Use when the user types /focused, or to enter a disciplined least-code mode for an implementation task.

availableCommands.name: ghost-infra
availableCommands.description: Hermes agent infrastructure and operations on yiin.lt. Hermes = NousResearch's hermes-agent (Python) — the old TypeScript "ghost" agent is permanently retired. Use when checking or restarting hermes-gateway/hermes-dashboard, viewing their logs, editing ~/.hermes/config.yaml, working with the dashboard at ghost.yiin.lt, or whenever "ghost", "Hermes", or "hermes-agent" comes up in an ops/deployment context.

availableCommands.name: graphify
availableCommands.description: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.

availableCommands.name: grill-with-docs
availableCommands.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADRs and glossary) as we go.

availableCommands.name: grilling
availableCommands.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan or design. Use when the user wants to stress-test a plan before building, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

availableCommands.name: hyperframes
availableCommands.description: Mandatory entry point: read this first for any request to make, create, edit, animate, or render a video, animation, or motion graphic, including a promo, explainer, captioned clip, title card, overlay, slideshow or interactive deck, Remotion port, or any HyperFrames HTML composition. Also use it to inspect, diagnose, validate, preview, publish, or batch-render an existing HyperFrames project. Inputs may be a website URL, GitHub PR, Figma design or URL, text or brief, existing footage, or music. It resumes project state, captures intent when applicable, selects and installs the owning workflow, and routes domain capabilities. HyperFrames is the default output framework unless the user explicitly chooses another framework for the deliverable or asks only to record a browser session.

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-animation
availableCommands.description: All animation knowledge for HyperFrames — atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, broader motion-design techniques, AND the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, plus Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations API, TypeGPU). Use for any motion or animation task: pick 2-4 rules and compose, or load a blueprint, or look up runtime-specific API (e.g. GSAP eases / Lottie player / Three.js mixer). Also covers auditing an existing composition's choreography (animation map) and 24 named text-animation effects. HyperFrames-native: single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic.

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-cli
availableCommands.description: Use the HyperFrames CLI development loop: init, add, catalog, capture, lint, check, snapshot, compare, grade-compare, preview, play, present, beats, keyframes, single or batch render, publish, cloud, cloudrun, feedback, lambda, doctor, browser, info, upgrade, skills, compositions, docs, benchmark, telemetry, transcribe, auth, tts, and remove-background. Also use when diagnosing build or render failures. validate, inspect, and layout are deprecated aliases; use check. Covers local, HeyGen-hosted cloud, AWS Lambda, and Google Cloud Run rendering.

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-core
availableCommands.description: The HyperFrames composition contract — build one renderable project. Use for composition structure, the `data-*` timing attributes, `class="clip"`, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, framework-owned media playback, deterministic-render rules, and validation. Also covers Tailwind projects and the STORYBOARD.md / SCRIPT.md plan formats. Read before writing composition HTML.

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-creative
availableCommands.description: Non-animation creative direction for HyperFrames videos. Use for design spec (frame.md / design.md) handling, palettes, typography, narration, beat planning, audio-reactive visuals, composition patterns, and brand / style decisions. For atomic motion patterns and scene blueprints, use `hyperframes-animation`.

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-keyframes
availableCommands.description: Use when a HyperFrames composition needs seek-safe 2D/3D keyframes, GSAP timelines, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG morph/draw, text trails, 3D depth, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics. Don't use for broad scene strategy, brand design, media sourcing, captions, or general video planning.

availableCommands.name: hyperframes-registry
availableCommands.description: Install, discover, and wire registry blocks and components into HyperFrames compositions. Use when running hyperframes add or hyperframes catalog, installing one item or every block matching a tag, wiring an installed item into index.html, or working with hyperframes.json. Covers discovery, install locations, block sub-composition wiring, component snippet merging, and authoring a new block or component to contribute upstream (idea → scaffold → validate → PR).

availableCommands.name: hypr-multiview
availableCommands.description: Configures and troubleshoots the Hyprland multi-view workspace system with headless monitors. Use when modifying hypr-multiview, workspace bindings, monitor configuration, or debugging workspace switching issues.

availableCommands.name: improve
availableCommands.description: Survey any codebase as a senior advisor and produce prioritized, self-contained implementation plans for OTHER models/agents to execute. Strictly read-only on source code — never implements, fixes, or refactors anything itself. Use when asked to audit a codebase, find improvement opportunities (bugs, security, performance, test coverage, tech debt, migrations, DX), suggest features or where to take the project next (roadmap, product direction), or generate handoff plans for another agent to implement.

availableCommands.name: improve-animations
availableCommands.description: Survey a codebase's animation and motion code as a senior motion advisor, then produce a prioritized audit and self-contained implementation plans for other agents (or cheaper models) to execute. Read-only on source code — it plans improvements, it does not apply them. Use when the user asks to "improve the animations", "audit the motion", "make this app feel better", or wants a roadmap of animation fixes rather than a review of a single diff.

availableCommands.name: improve-codebase-architecture
availableCommands.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

availableCommands.name: init
availableCommands.description: guided AGENTS.md setup

availableCommands.name: install-anti-slop
availableCommands.description: Install and configure the anti-slop Oxlint plugin in a local TypeScript or JavaScript repository. Use whenever a user asks to add anti-slop lint rules, copy the anti-slop plugin, configure opinionated Oxlint rules, or migrate an existing local anti-slop setup.

availableCommands.name: investigate-bundles-issue
availableCommands.description: End-to-end handling of a Kaching Bundles bug/issue — deep investigation that validates assumptions against the real code, a skeptical check on whether it belongs in our codebase at all, then /focused /cook-it the fix, then open a PR with a description in the writing-clearly-and-concisely voice. Use when the user points at a bundles issue (a Linear PRO-* ticket, a Slack/Intercom report, or a prose bug description) and wants it taken from "what's going on" all the way to "PR is up". Triggers on "/investigate-bundles-issue <ref>", or "investigate and fix <bundles bug>, open a PR".

availableCommands.name: lavish
availableCommands.description: Turn complex or visual agent responses into rich, reviewable HTML artifacts the user can annotate and send feedback on, using the lavish-axi CLI. Use when about to give a plan, comparison, diagram, table, code diff, report, or anything easier to grasp visually than as prose.

availableCommands.name: manage-power-plan
availableCommands.description: Manages power profiles on this Arch Linux machine using powerprofilesctl. Use when the user wants to switch power modes (power-saver, balanced, performance), check current power state, optimize battery life, or boost performance. Also use when the user says things like "low power mode", "save battery", "full performance", or asks about CPU governors, EPP, or platform profiles.

availableCommands.name: media-use
availableCommands.description: Agent Media OS, the single skill for every media need in a HyperFrames project. Resolve BGM, SFX, image, icon, brand logo, voice, color grade, or LUT into a frozen local file or paste-ready block + ledger record (one verb, `resolve`); generate via TTS / music / image models when the catalog misses; produce voiceover, transcription, captions, and background removal through one shared audio engine; operate on media (cut / reframe / transform); and reuse assets across projects. Also use for vague feedback that real footage looks dark, flat, boring, should feel retro/camcorder/print/ASCII, needs privacy, or needs a media reveal.

availableCommands.name: migrate-to-shoehorn
availableCommands.description: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.

availableCommands.name: plan-epic
availableCommands.description: Plan a large piece of work as a beads epic — investigate the subject in depth with a fan-out of agents, create the epic and its child issues, then write a self-contained handoff protocol into the epic itself so /cook-epic runs it end-to-end without a separate HANDOFF.md. Use when the user types /plan-epic, or asks to plan, scope, or break down an epic, feature, or large task into beads issues.

availableCommands.name: playwright-cli
availableCommands.description: Automate browser interactions, test web pages and work with Playwright tests.

availableCommands.name: playwright-trace
availableCommands.description: Inspect Playwright trace files from the command line — list actions, view requests, console, errors, snapshots and screenshots.

availableCommands.name: product-launch-video
availableCommands.description: Turn a product or marketing URL, pasted script, or brief into a product launch / promo video — SaaS promos, feature reveals, product demos, app and company launches. Use when the user wants to market, launch, promote, or reveal a product; the default for any commercial URL. Site tours / showcases of a website route here too — the brief carries the show-it-as-is intent. Unclear → /hyperframes.

availableCommands.name: ralph
availableCommands.description: Run a fresh-context agent loop (Ralph pattern) using the same CLI harness that invoked the skill—Codex launches `codex exec`, Claude Code and ccx launch `claude -p`, Kimi Code launches `kimi -p`, and OpenCode launches `opencode run`. Each iteration starts with empty context; state lives in the repo (handoff file, beads, git). Use when the user types /ralph followed by a loop prompt.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: review changes [commit|branch|pr], defaults to uncommitted

availableCommands.name: review-animations
availableCommands.description: Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

availableCommands.name: sec-status
availableCommands.description: Investigate security pipeline candidates on travel-laptop and yiin-lt and give the user a plain-language status report on suspicious activity. Use when the user types /sec-status, asks "anything sus?", wants a security status check, or asks whether the security pipeline flagged anything.

availableCommands.name: sniff
availableCommands.description: Analyze a REST Sniffer timeline JSON file from ~/Downloads. Use when the user types /sniff <filename> to load and analyze a captured browser session timeline (network requests + DOM/click/frame/script events) produced by the Sniffer Chrome DevTools extension.

availableCommands.name: spin-up-dashboard
availableCommands.description: Provision and extend project dashboards on yiin-lt with Yiin/dashboards. Use when creating, recreating, or changing an instance, harness, workspace module, tailnet route, or dashboard surface.

availableCommands.name: sync-bd
availableCommands.description: Wire the current project's beads (bd) database to the shared Dolt server on yiin-lt so both machines share one live copy. Use when initing beads for a new project, connecting a fresh clone, migrating a legacy embedded database, or diagnosing "No beads database" / connection-refused / identity-mismatch errors. Trigger with /sync-bd from the project root.

availableCommands.name: system-management
availableCommands.description: Manages and documents system-level changes on this Arch Linux laptop (Lenovo 82WQ). Use when troubleshooting or configuring audio, display, networking, power, kernel, drivers, systemd services, or any hardware/OS-level issue. Tracks all changes in ~/.local/share/system-docs/.

availableCommands.name: ui-ux-pro-max
availableCommands.description: UI/UX design intelligence for web and mobile. Includes 50+ styles, 161 color palettes, 57 font pairings, 161 product types, 99 UX guidelines, and 25 chart types across 10 stacks (React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, SwiftUI, React Native, Flutter, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, and HTML/CSS). Actions: plan, build, create, design, implement, review, fix, improve, optimize, enhance, refactor, and check UI/UX code. Projects: website, landing page, dashboard, admin panel, e-commerce, SaaS, portfolio, blog, and mobile app. Elements: button, modal, navbar, sidebar, card, table, form, and chart. Styles: glassmorphism, claymorphism, minimalism, brutalism, neumorphism, bento grid, dark mode, responsive, skeuomorphism, and flat design. Topics: color systems, accessibility, animation, layout, typography, font pairing, spacing, interaction states, shadow, and gradient. Integrations: shadcn/ui MCP for component search and examples.

availableCommands.name: use-betaflight
availableCommands.description: Configure FPV drones and radios over USB — Betaflight flight controllers (modes/AUX channels, beeper, GPS Rescue/RTH, CLI settings) and EdgeTX radios (switch→channel mixes on the TX16S and similar). Use whenever the task touches Betaflight, an FC/flight controller, arming or flight modes, a beeper or turtle/flip-over switch, GPS Rescue or return-to-home, ELRS/ExpressLRS binding or channel mapping, or editing an EdgeTX/OpenTX model. Invoke BEFORE poking a serial port or the Betaflight web app so you don't leave the FC in a broken state.

availableCommands.name: use-bundles-prod
availableCommands.description: Connect to the Kaching Bundles production Rails server on Render over SSH to run READ-ONLY Rails console queries. Use when you need to inspect live production data for the bundles app — a shop, deal block, feature flag, subscription, order, or any model — to debug an issue, verify a hypothesis, or check adoption. READ-ONLY ONLY; any write needs explicit user confirmation first.

availableCommands.name: use-cloudflare
availableCommands.description: Manages Cloudflare resources via the REST API. Use when creating, listing, updating, or deleting zones, DNS records, page rules, firewall rules, cache settings, Workers, R2 buckets, or any other Cloudflare infrastructure. Also use when purging cache, managing SSL/TLS settings, configuring redirects, or checking zone analytics.

availableCommands.name: use-coolify
availableCommands.description: Manage Coolify self-hosted PaaS on the VPS (yiin.lt). Use when deploying, inspecting, or managing applications, databases, services, environment variables, or server resources via the Coolify API. Also use when checking deployment logs or troubleshooting hosted services.

availableCommands.name: use-digitalocean
availableCommands.description: Manage DigitalOcean infrastructure via the doctl CLI. Use when creating, listing, updating, or deleting droplets, domains, DNS records, databases, volumes, load balancers, firewalls, VPCs, SSH keys, projects, snapshots, Kubernetes clusters, or App Platform apps.

availableCommands.name: use-discord
availableCommands.description: Read-only search and browse of the user's personal Discord (DMs, group DMs, joined servers) via the `discord-search` CLI. Use when the user asks to find, list, recall, or look up Discord messages, channels, DMs, or servers — e.g. "search my Discord DMs for X", "what did <person> say about Y", "find that link <friend> sent me", "list the servers I'm in", "show recent messages in channel Z". The CLI is intentionally read-only (no send/edit/delete).

availableCommands.name: use-github
availableCommands.description: Manages GitHub repositories, issues, PRs, releases, Actions, and settings via the gh CLI. Use when creating, listing, updating, or deleting repos, issues, pull requests, releases, gists, or managing Actions workflows, secrets, deploy keys, branch protection, and other GitHub resources.

availableCommands.name: use-hetzner
availableCommands.description: Manages Hetzner infrastructure — Cloud resources via the hcloud CLI (servers, networks, firewalls, volumes, floating IPs, load balancers, DNS zones, SSH keys) and dedicated servers via the Robot API (rescue mode, reset, installimage, traffic, reverse DNS). Use when creating, listing, modifying, or deleting any Hetzner resource, provisioning servers, or working with a dedicated/Robot box that does not appear in the Cloud console.

availableCommands.name: use-heymantle-docs
availableCommands.description: Reference for the Mantle App API (heymantle.com) v1.0 — full OpenAPI schema for every REST endpoint (identify, customer, subscriptions, one-time charges, usage events, invoices, affiliates, hosted sessions, discounts, notifications) plus all 30 Mantle webhook topics (plans/*, subscriptions/*, customers/*, contacts/*, transactions/*, etc.). Use whenever writing, reviewing, or debugging Mantle API calls, designing Mantle webhook handlers, picking the right endpoint, checking required headers/params/body fields, decoding a webhook payload, or resolving a 401/404 from `appapi.heymantle.com`. Triggers on mentions of Mantle, heymantle, `X-Mantle-App-Id`, `X-Mantle-App-Api-Key`, `X-Mantle-Customer-Api-Token`, `appapi.heymantle.com`, `/identify`, `mantleClient`, `@heymantle/client`, or any Mantle endpoint/webhook-topic name.

availableCommands.name: use-intercom
availableCommands.description: Read and search Intercom conversations, contacts, and tags via the REST API. Use when an Intercom conversation link is shared, when you need to read customer messages, or when pulling/analyzing Kaching support conversations by tag, agent, or theme.

availableCommands.name: use-linear
availableCommands.description: Browse and manage Linear workspaces (issues, projects, comments, documents, initiatives, milestones, cycles, teams, users, attachments) via Linear's official MCP server. Use when listing/searching/filtering Linear issues, changing status, assigning, commenting, creating/updating issues or projects, or inspecting any workspace object. Triggers on mentions of Linear, any Linear issue identifier (e.g. DEV-123, ENG-42), "move issue to X", "assign to me", "list my Linear tickets", Linear projects/initiatives/milestones/cycles, or any Linear workflow task.

availableCommands.name: use-namecheap
availableCommands.description: Manages Namecheap domains and DNS via the REST API. Use when creating, listing, updating, or deleting DNS records, managing domains, checking availability, renewing domains, configuring nameservers, managing SSL certificates, domain privacy, or user addresses on Namecheap-registered domains.

availableCommands.name: use-notes
availableCommands.description: Manage the personal TriliumNext notes instance at https://notes.yiin.lt via its ETAPI REST API. Use whenever the user mentions Trilium, notes.yiin.lt, "my notes", saving or looking something up in notes, filing information under a project (Yiin MB, Accounting, Maximo, Proga, Vangrd, KachingAppz), journaling/day notes, or wants an agent to record findings, meeting notes, or accounting records durably — even when they never say "Trilium". Also use for searching, reorganizing, exporting, or backing up notes, and for wiring other agents/scripts to the notes API.

availableCommands.name: use-porkbun
availableCommands.description: Manages Porkbun domains and DNS via the REST API. Use when creating, listing, updating, or deleting DNS records, managing domains, checking availability, retrieving SSL certificates, or configuring URL forwarding on Porkbun-registered domains.

availableCommands.name: use-proga-auth0
availableCommands.description: Manages Proga's Auth0 tenant via the Management API. Use when configuring applications, grant types, callback URLs, API audiences, connections, users, roles, or troubleshooting authentication issues for the Proga event management platform.

availableCommands.name: use-proga-mailserver
availableCommands.description: Connect to and operate the proga.lt mail server — a mailcow-dockerized host on Hetzner serving mail for proga.lt (webmail/admin at mail.proga.lt). Use when SSHing into the mail server, managing mailboxes/aliases/domains, checking or changing its DNS auth records (SPF/DKIM/DMARC/BIMI/MX/PTR), debugging mail delivery or deliverability, renewing certs, updating or restarting mailcow, or anything touching proga.lt email. Triggers on "proga mail", "mail.proga.lt", "proga.lt email/mailbox", mailcow on proga, or a proga.lt mail deliverability question.

availableCommands.name: use-proxycheap
availableCommands.description: Manages Proxy-Cheap proxy services via the REST API. Use when listing, ordering, configuring, or managing proxies — residential, datacenter, mobile, rotating. Also use when checking proxy status, whitelisting IPs, changing protocols, extending periods, or buying bandwidth.

availableCommands.name: use-render
availableCommands.description: Manages Render cloud resources via the REST API. Use when creating, listing, updating, or deleting services, deploys, databases, environment variables, custom domains, disks, blueprints, cron jobs, or any other Render infrastructure. Also use when triggering deploys, checking logs, scaling services, or managing environment groups.

availableCommands.name: use-resend
availableCommands.description: Sends transactional emails via the Resend API. Use when sending emails (password resets, notifications, verifications), managing domains/DNS for deliverability, or working with contacts and audiences.

availableCommands.name: use-rpi
availableCommands.description: Work with the Raspberry Pi 4B running Arch Linux ARM with an Omarchy-ported Hyprland desktop, reachable via USB-C gadget ethernet from travel-laptop, home WiFi, or tailnet (rpi / 100.115.233.27). Use whenever the user says "rpi", "the pi", "raspberry", or asks to run/install/check anything on the Raspberry Pi, show its screen, fix its boot config, or troubleshoot why it is unreachable — even if they don't mention USB, VNC, or tailscale.

availableCommands.name: use-shopify-dev
availableCommands.description: Reference for the Shopify Admin GraphQL API (version 2026-04) — full schema for every query, mutation, object, input-object, payload, enum, connection, interface, union, and scalar. Use this skill whenever the user is writing, reviewing, or debugging Shopify Admin GraphQL queries/mutations, looking up field/argument types, deciding which mutation to call, resolving GraphQL validation errors, planning paginated queries, working with Shopify metafields/products/orders/customers/discounts/fulfillment/inventory/checkout via the Admin API, mentions `shopify.dev`, `admin-graphql`, `kachingappz` Shopify code, the `shopify_api` Ruby gem, or `@shopify/shopify-api` Node SDK. Triggers on phrases like "Shopify GraphQL", "Admin API mutation", "what fields does X object have", "ProductInput", "fulfillmentOrders", "metafieldsSet", or any Shopify GraphQL type/query/mutation name.

availableCommands.name: use-stripe
availableCommands.description: Manages Stripe resources via the Stripe CLI. Use when creating, listing, or modifying customers, products, prices, subscriptions, payment intents, invoices, or other Stripe API objects. Also use for webhook testing, event monitoring, log tailing, fixture-based automation, and Stripe project configuration.

availableCommands.name: use-tailscale
availableCommands.description: Manage and troubleshoot Tailscale (the WireGuard mesh VPN / tailnet) via the tailscale CLI. Invoke this skill BEFORE doing anything that touches Tailscale, even indirectly. Triggers: any mention of Tailscale, a tailnet, MagicDNS, exit nodes, Tailscale SSH, serve/funnel, or Taildrop file transfer; switching tailnets/accounts/profiles; reaching — or failing to reach — a tailnet node (the NAS `kami-sama-nas`, the `yiin` VPS, another laptop); questions like "which tailnet am I on", "why can't I reach <device>", "add this machine to <tailnet>", or "give me a login link"; AND the less-obvious cases — a git fetch/push/clone/pull over SSH that fails to resolve or reach a `*.ts.net` host, any "Could not resolve hostname ...ts.net" or tailnet-DNS error, or an SSH/HTTP call to a 100.x address that hangs or refuses. Invoke it even when the user never names the `tailscale` CLI and even when the surface symptom looks like a git or network failure rather than a Tailscale one.

availableCommands.name: use-travel-laptop
availableCommands.description: Connect to and manage the travel laptop (ASUS ZenBook S16, hostname travel-laptop) — a near-mirror Omarchy/Arch machine. Use when SSHing into it, running commands on it, troubleshooting its hardware/boot/GPU, syncing configs or projects to it, or any task that targets the travel/secondary laptop rather than this main machine. Triggers on "travel laptop", "the ZenBook", "travel-laptop", "the other laptop", or "the second machine".

availableCommands.name: use-voice
availableCommands.description: Speak to the user out loud instead of writing text, using the ElevenLabs API and the local `voice` CLI. Use when an agent needs to reach the user away from the keyboard: a long task just finished, a run is blocked and needs a decision, a background job failed, or the user asked to be told something rather than shown it. Also use for any request to say, speak, read aloud, voice, narrate, or generate an audio or MP3 message, or to change the notification voice.

availableCommands.name: use-webflow
availableCommands.description: Manages Webflow resources via the REST API. Use when creating, listing, updating, or deleting sites, pages, CMS collections, collection items, assets, forms, users, ecommerce products/orders, webhooks, or custom code. Also use when publishing sites or CMS items, managing page SEO/metadata, or working with Webflow localization.

availableCommands.name: verify-against-shopify-themes
availableCommands.description: Check whether a storefront change (widget, theme-extension, injected DOM/JS) works across the most popular Shopify themes, weighted by the app's real install base. Fans out one subagent per top theme/family to source-verify each theme's relevant markup + JS, traces the change's "theme contract" against it, and returns an install-base-weighted coverage report plus the gaps worth fixing. User-invocable only: run when the user explicitly types /verify-against-shopify-themes. Do not invoke proactively.

availableCommands.name: wayfinder
availableCommands.description: Plan a huge chunk of work — more than one agent session can hold — as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

availableCommands.name: web-recon
availableCommands.description: Playwright-based web reconnaissance and scraping. Use when navigating websites, intercepting network requests/responses, understanding authentication flows, scraping webapp content, or building automation scripts from observed browser traffic. Triggers on any task involving browsing a site to understand its API surface, capturing authenticated requests, login-and-scrape workflows, or generating Playwright scripts from live interaction. Even if the user just says "go to X and grab Y", this skill applies.

availableCommands.name: webdev
availableCommands.description: Web development testing and debugging using Playwright (functional validation) and Chrome DevTools (debugging). Use when testing web apps — clicking through flows, verifying navigation, checking renders, inspecting console errors, analyzing network requests, profiling performance, or running Lighthouse audits. Also handles "local overrides" — swapping production resources (JS/CSS/JSON) for local dev builds in real browser context, to verify a fix on a live site before shipping. Supports a headless mode (no visible windows) for batch checks across many sites. Triggers on: "test this page", "check if X works", "debug why Y isn't rendering", "run a lighthouse audit", "check console errors", "profile performance", "verify the login flow", "test my local fix on prod", "override prod script with my build", "run headless", "without opening a window", or any web app QA/debugging task.

availableCommands.name: working-on-design
availableCommands.description: Single entry point for all UI/UX design work — building or restyling interfaces, aesthetic direction, animation and motion, gestures, charts, accessibility. Routes to the right specialist layer and loads only what the task needs. Use for any task that changes how a feature looks, feels, moves, or is interacted with (e.g. `/cook-it <feature> use /working-on-design`).

availableCommands.name: working-on-local-bundles
availableCommands.description: Work efficiently against the local Kaching Bundles dev environment (shopify app dev + dev store) — drive the embedded admin as the user, query/mutate the dev store via the CLI GraphiQL proxy, verify storefront widget behavior, and avoid the App Bridge / metafield / CI gotchas that waste hours without context. Use when developing, testing, or e2e-verifying features on a kaching-bundles-dev store (admin editor, storefront widget, deal blocks, metafields).

availableCommands.name: writing-clearly-and-concisely
availableCommands.description: Plain, human writing for any prose people will read — documentation, guides, PR descriptions, commit messages, error messages, UI copy, changelogs, reports. Also use when editing or reviewing text to remove AI-writing patterns (this absorbs the old humanizer skill). Not for agent status reports to the user (that's STE100, see the explain skill).
